Rules: There is only one rule. The rule is, there must be at least one of everything in the map. And not just enemies, either. There needs to be at least one of every single tile as well. It doesn't matter what way they face. As well as one of every tile, you also need at least one of every enemy, and everything else like bounce blocks etc. Also, they all must be visible otherwise the map will be disqualified.

Each person is allowed to submit up to 3 maps if they wish.

POST HERE TO JOIN! PM ME TO JOIN AND BE A JUDGE!

ALSO, Judges are allowed to enter, but they have to judge their own maps fairly.

NOTE: The contest finishes on the 20th Febuary so make sure all entries are in well before then!
Judging will then commence and go for approximately a week.


Here are the images you can add to your signatures if you wish.





If you're both a compedator and a jugde, feel free to animaring userbar from my signature.

EDIT: Oh, I forgot the judging criteria! Maps will be judged on:
How it looks /5
Use of enemies and other objects /5
Difficulty /5 NOTE: Difficulty is not ranged from easy to hard or anything like that. Judge it on how completable it is, but not too easy. Know what I mean?
Creativity /10
"Funness" /15
Gameplay /20

TOTAL: /60
The judges' marks will be averaged to form the end mark.


Prizes: 1st place: A dedication and a signature bar.
2nd place: A Signature.
3rd place: Another signature


Judges: Me (Weisslenny0) ....... Easy going. You'll be getting at least 40/60 from me, unless your level really really sucks...
Sephorith ....... Rock Solid. Better make a good level if you want more that 30/60!


Contestants: Me (Weisslenny0)
Sephorith
Max_ride
Fingersonthefrets
Hypnotizer
Epigone
Ali_2


Hope you all have a great time!!!

#13602 1 2007-01-20T05:51:46Z Weisslenny0
Welcome to the userbar and signature competition!

Basically this is a competition where anyone who likes creating userbars or signatures can create two per week according to the weekly specifications and submit them here. NOTE: You are allowed to change your entries during the week.
The top 3 entries each week will win a userbar that they can put into their signature. They will get to choose the colors of the userbar and how they change from one to the other.
The winner of each week will also get a level dedicated to them.

JUDGING: There will be four criteria for judging:
1: Use of color(s) n/10
2: Creativity n/10
3: Use of the week's theme n/10
4: "Just looking at it" n/10 (basically this is for how good it looks when you just look at it. Hence the name.

Judges' marks will be averaged and the winning 3 entries will be posted here.

Judges[/u] will rate each and every picture in the week after it closes. All judgings must be emailed to me within 5 days of the week's entries closing.

Specifications for userbars and signatures:
All Userbars MUST be no bigger than 400X20 pixels.
All Signatures MUST be no bigger than 400X200 pixels.
EDIT: I changed the size. Signatures can now be 10 times taller than userbars. You can go over this size, but I (and possibly other judges) will penalize you.

If you wish to join this competition, post here saying so!

TOPIC FOR WEEK 4:
Team battles. This is for the whole game of N. Basically, get two (or more) teams of enemies from N and have them battling in some way. Any use of weapons allowed, like maybe having N shooting a chaingun or something. Each team must have at least 2 "characters" and you're allowed to use each character more than once.

---Previous weeks---

WEEK 3:
Good Ol' Fashioned Fighting. This can be the whole game of N or just the little character N. You choose.
This has to have something to do with N (either the game or the Ninja) and also something to do with fighting, and all melee fighting at that. You're allowed to use things like knives, swords, hand-to-hand combat, maybe even a matrix sort of thing, with no guns or weapons developed after 1800.
You may, however, have laser drones and chaingun drones, as long as they aren't shooting.
Feel free to use N poser to get some nice poses of hand-to-hand combat if you're doing that.

A reminder that entries will be back to 2 per week from now on, unless I say otherwise.

This week will end on Sunday the 11th of Feb, at midnight GMT.


WEEK TWO:
N Sports! Yes, the whole game of N!
Make your picture something to do with N, and something to do with sport. For example, you could have two Ns with little tennis rackets and the ball could be a floor guard. Or, If you're good at 3D, you could have a picture of N wolding a gold club which looks 3D!
Experiment with the topic, and remember: You are allowed to submt 3 (YES, THREE!!!) entries this week because it's so long.
Feel free to use whatever you want to get pictures of N and enemies etc. Please have things that are form the game though. No made-up drones.

This week ends on the 4th of February.



WEEK ONE:
N. Not the whole game though, just N. Try and cram as much about N as you can into your userbar or signature!
NOTE: It's fine if you have N getting shot or his blood or something like that in there, as long as you DON'T have the enemy that shot him as well!
NOTE 2 (too, get it? It's a bad pun...): You are allowed to use any programs to get N. You can draw him in an N art if you want, then put it in your signature or userbar. Whatever you think is good, as long as it has N.
ALSO, your entry will NOT be disqualified if you have other things in the image, but it is likely to recieve less marks in the "weeks theme" criteria.

Week one ends on Sunday the 28th at Midnight GMT.


Members: Me (Weisslenny0)
Hypnotizer
Motocrosser
Chasethebase
Hendor

Judges: Me (Weisslenny0)
Sephorith (Not week 1)
29403

TO JUDGES: Email me at weissl2001@hotmail.com if you would like any different colours for your userbar.


I think that's about it. PM me or email me if there's anything I've left out!

Good Luck to everyone, and ENJOY!!!

But can't you just delete the #DS# or something like that at the beginning of the level data? I think I tried that with one of my levels and it worked.
For SUBLiME submissions, the number of tiles horizontally and vertically is different than in regular N:


original: 33x25
ds: 34x26
psp: 32x19
xbla: 35x27

So in the case of DS, regular N might show a playable map if you just cut off the $DS### but you're losing a bunch of tiles (because the DS map size is one row+column larger), so you won't be getting the whole thing. Know what I mean?

#370907 8 2007-10-09T23:58:28Z Weisslenny0
Ah, this is the other topic that I haven't commented on. Wow, 5 songs to do. OK, here we go...

Force Majeure
Nice start; the accidentals are interesting. I really liked the piece when there was only about 1 minute to go, because it combines the original melody with awesome percussion. When it got to 20 secs left I was really feeling the beat etc., and I like the way that it can loop well.

Hexaplex
Interesting start. Much slower than Force Majeure, but I liked it. I liked the percussion when there was only 50 or so second left. It really added to the melody. Again, good ending; nice and loopable.

Red Telephone
Ah, a longer piece. Again an interesting start; it started off like a scale, but it wasn't. Interesting. I liked when the melody came in after about 30 secs and the chords really added to it. In general the piece just got better as it went along. I think that the faster notes could be a bit louder so they stand out more though. I liked when the faster still notes came in after 2 or so mins because they added to the melody, then it went back to the original and that sounded really nice. It got interesting at the end because it changed, but I just thought it would repeat. Not sure that the fade-out worked - I think it would have been better if it looped.

Vive Cathodique!
I really liked this piece, and the beginning especially . It just got really nice once the 2nd instrument came in with quavers; in one way it was a slow piece but another fast, and I really liked that. Then the guitar-like instrument came in, and it added to the melody nicely. Currently there's just over a minute left and there's the awesome melody with the guitar, and that's awesome. Then another instrument (glockenspiel?) comes in, and that's even more awesome . Hmm, interesting end. TGhe melody changes, but it's repeatable I think, and sounds really good. In short, I added it to my iTunes "awesome music" playlist .

Qubcois Folk Hero
Nice beat at the beginning. I was tapping the beat, and that was fun . I like how it starts of slowly melody-wise, but the actual piece is fast. The synth is awesome too; I liked it. Currently just over 2 minutes left and it's still sounding really good. I can imagine this being in a sort of space-like level or something - not evil boss music, but would work well for levels. Now just over a minute left and the guitar sounds really nice. I like how the melody works, and the slide in the chords also works, and more importantly they worked together. The fade-out at the end was good this time, but not for game purposes, I think. Still, good to have a loopable track that fades out.

And just a general comment for all the pieces, they all sound like awesome game music. And thanks for giving me an enjoyable time listening to them
Lenny

#381186 10 2007-11-20T08:45:21Z Weisslenny0
Quote: LittleViking001, November 19, 2007 10:50 am
There's a cool glitch that allows this that I've never seen anyone use. It might take some planning to get the exact drone path you want, but it can be done. In the tile data, if you replace a character with *, the tile in that position acts as solid to zap drones (and thwumps) but acts like an empty space to everything else, including the ninja. So if you put these zap-solid tiles at the corners of the path you want, it'll follow that path without interrupting the rest of the level.

Load a blank map first for full effect; the * tiles don't draw over whatever was there before, so if it was another map, it'll look like there are tiles where there are none.

Awesome, that is so cool!

And I thought something like this had been suggested before, and the result was that it would be annoying to code, and better just to stick with what there is. Or is that just me...

#18276 1 2007-12-05T03:59:49Z Weisslenny0
Hey Everyone,

Firstly, I'll tell you the point of this important announcement. On the 16th of December I'm going on holidays to New Zealand for 5 or 6 weeks, and I won't have internet access. So, I wanted to make sure that everyone has something to do (even if small) while I'm away.

So, my question is, Do you have anything to do?
If you don't, and are unsure on what you're meant to be doing, check the Roster. If you are still unsure on what you're doing, post something here telling me or one of the other mods. And if the roster information is wrong, please post something there telling me.
If you know what you're meant to be doing, but don't have a composer/performer/editor, post something in the Request Topic so we can get it sorted out ASAP.
If there is anything you're unsure about with Metastra in general, check the General Discussion to see if there's already a similar question. If there's not, please ask it there.

Note for everyone: Please Check the Request Topic regularly, and please volunteer if you can do what someone is asking! Also, if you're on the forums, just drop by this sub-forum regularly. I know it's not easy to find nowadays, but it really helps if everyone knows what's happening. You could also get up to date with the news by going onto the IRC Channel (#Metastra), where there should be someone who can help you. And if you've got some free time, please listen to others' compositions or recordings to see what you think.
Notes for composers: If you've thought of a great song, why not compose it for instruments in Metastra! That way you can request people to play it for you too!
Notes for performers: If you've got any time, improvise. See if you can come up with anything that could be useful, then record it and ask a composer to do something interesting with it.
Notes for editors: You guys are really important. It's your job to make sure that all the pieces have been recorded properly and fit together nicely. If one part is out of time or tune, post something in that topic telling people, so it can be fixed.

Now, I think I've covered everything. If there's something you think I've missed out on in this post, please tell me ASAP so I can add it in.

Thanks, and I hope to see everyone organized before I leave.

Lenny

Quote: crappitrash, December 14, 2007 11:22 pm
A single movement for string quartet. Had everyone who played it complaining about "WTF, five flats?!"

Hahaha
Sorry

When writing for strings, it's generally a good idea to write the whole thing with one sharp (G major) or two sharps (D major).
Why? A violin has a G string and a D string, a viola has a G string and a D string (an octave lower), a cello has a G string and a D string (again, another octave lower), and a double bass (if you're using this) has that same G string, and a D string a fourth lower than that.
Trust me on this one; it's hard for a stringed instrument to even play three flats, let-alone 5.

Untitled (I like F Minor)
Interesting start. I liked the use of the piano and snare. It gave it the beat which I couldn't really feel at the beginning. Plus, nice relaxed feel. Not too fast, nor to slow... Personal note: Never listen to maestro's music while Mum's around. She will start dancing. I'm not sure if that's a complement or not.

Hyperchords
Hum, shorter song. Nice though; just a good feel to it, and a nice melody. Woah, weird at 30 secs . This wasn't so... cool. I don't know, I just didn't really like some of the chords here. Supermassive Black Hole (Remix)

Shipping Bells

#402285 2 2008-01-20T10:25:54Z Weisslenny0
It's quite simple, really.

Up at the top of the screen, you'll see a button that reads "My Controls". Click this. On that page, look to the left. Under 'Personal Profile' is the text "Edit Signature" (http://metanet.2.forumer.com/index.php?act=UserCP&CODE=22). Then scroll down and just type stuff into the text box. Press "update my signature" when you're done, and you will have a signature.

If you're unsure of other things, like adding colors, pictures, and whatever, don't hesitate to PM me (click the "PM" button under my name) and I'll be more than happy to answer. Enjoy!

You might also wish to get a small signature and/or avatar (you can request one in Images) so people can identify you easily. It's also a good idea to link to things that you're talking about, as opposed to saying "go find this", and if you're unsure about stuff, nicely PM one of the moderators, and they'll get back to you soon. I'd say PM me, but I probably wouldn't be very helpful.

#404134 26 2008-01-25T22:39:09Z Weisslenny0
OK, here goes then...

I've organised the following like this:
NAME (in bold)
Listening through (what I felt)
Summary (if I like it or not, a rough rating/10, or something similar)

Oh, and any unrelated commantary is in blue.

Technically Frozen
Nice start. Which, although it has rests, gave a good sense of the beat. 20 secs in: Nice melody line. I liked how it went from action-y to relaxed, and back again. Nice ending, also.
Basically, I like this song. If this wasn't already in iTunes, I'd put it in now. Somewhere around a 9.5/10, if not higher.

Synth Stager
Interesting start. I like the drone, with the added notes above it. Then when the percussion comes in, it starts sounding really good. I would have possibly made slight variotions of the percussion melody, but that's just me. 1 min in; This sounds good. The lower instrument sounds a but funny to me, but the higher one works well. Good fade-out ending.
Hmm.. interesting. I don't think I liked it as much as Technically Frozen, but it was still pretty cool. Maybe 7/10?

Quartz Boulder
Nice chords, added to be the drum beat. I liked the little synth that came in, too. 30 secs in, nice use of the cymbals, and then again at the end with the drum, too. Good fade-out, too. It worked well.
Pretty cool, yeah. Maybe 7 or 8.

Progressive Norse, Of Course
Nice violin melody, and nice implementation of the electric guitar and drums. 30 secs in; nice use of the bongos, while geeping the electric guitar chords. I liked that. 55 secs in; oh, bongos and melody, nice! Then good use of rests, while keeping the bongos on. And good fade-out of the electric guitar.
I liked it. Probably hovering around an 8 somewhere.

Mining For Ghosts
Nice start. The beat can be felt well, and good implementation of the cymbals. They work really well just being soft. 35 secs in; nice piano usage, then on to steel (?) guitar. I liked that, and then with the piano chords later. Not sure if the piano chord worked at the end though.
Mmm... good. 7 or 8, again.

~~~ Phew, half way through. Let's take a break...
~~~ OK, break time's over. Let's get back to this!

Machinery
Nice, rhythmical start. I can see why it's called "Machinery". Nice low synth. This gave the music a more electronic feel. The higher synth sounds a bit funny though, though maybe it's just me. 55 secs in; ooh, this is nice. Vaguely underwater feel. I like that. 1:20 in; Interesting synth here, which fits the melody well. Both of them do, in fact. I liked how the ending went back to the beginning, sorta. That was good.
Again, 8ish.

Headache
Nice guitar melody, which is added to nicely by the bass. Interesting percussion though. It works, but I think it's too loud, possibly. For me, it blocks out too much of the melody. 45 secs in; Nice lower instrument. Well, it's not that low, actually, but it's nice. Again, I liked the way the piece went back to the beginning, with only guitar.
Hmm... maybe... 7ish. Bit higher. Sorta 7.5/10.

Ground Wire
Nice drums at the beginning, and I liked the guitar playing soon after. It's funny; although the beats occasionally conflict, you can still feel the beat really well. 50 secs in; I like the use of the percussion and the melody here. The two went together well, and the drums help the slight change there. The ending was good, though I think it cut back to one instrument to quickly.
Perhaps around 8 somewhere, yet again.

Exoticoustic
Yay, guitar again. I liked the melody that it played, and the percussion and the other instrument really added to this melody. I love the bass, too, 30 secs in. It sorta feels like it gets drowned out by the guitar strumming though, but that fades out nicely to end.
I'd go about 9, I think. I liked it.

Blue Ice
sweet synth action here. The percussion really works, and nice tango feel with the piano, followed by the synths some more. I really liked how you could feel the beat the whole way through. That made me happy. Interesting fade-out at the end, though I think it worked well.
Slightly higher than 9. Maybe.. 9.2ish/10. Could have been a bit longer though, because it's the only song under a minute

~~~ Looking back over this, it looks like I may have focused more on the bad than the good. I just want to say that all the songs are, actually, really good, and I strongly encourage everyone to listen to Quartz Boulder.
~~~ Also, I appreciate the time that's gone into these, and thankyou tons for sharing these with everyone. To show my appreciation, you get a smiley!
~~~ (OK, more than one smiley.)

And you're welcome for all the comments. You did ask, after all.

Well, I figured that seeing as Matt's still getting back on his feet, and no one's talked about where this is going or what's happening, I'd try and organize something.

Status: All PMs sent, now waiting for all replies to come in.

What I propose will happen is the following:
All performers shall PM me, stating that they either A) Have an original song which they can perform, or B) Don't have a song to perform and would like one. If A is they case, I'd like the performer to at least look at the piece, see if they can play though it, etc. It only takes five minutes.
All composers shall PM me, stating that either A) They have composed something, or B) They haven't. If B is the case, I shall PM you back with some specifications for your composition soon.
All editors Shall sit back and relax, until I PM you with something that needs editing.
If you are doing more than one of these, please mention this in the PM and state A or B (if necessary).

N.B. I'd like it if everyone in this could be checking this forum every few days, as I'll hopefully be updating The Request Topic every few days, and PMing you about what you need to do, and by when. If this all works out well enough, most discussion may be able to take place in a topic.

Also, if Matt, Borealis or Sendy thinks that this is a bad idea, I shall stop. But please tell me to do so.

Something else important: as soon as you read this, PM me about it so you don't forget. It only takes a minute to say, "Hey, this is Lenny (or your name...), and I have done some composing, but not my performing." or whatever the case is for you.

Hate to be all "do this, do that...", but I want this forum to keep moving.

Sweet, an OS topic.

Personally, I like Windows XP. I looked at Vista, and it was too different. I did like Inkball (game), though.
It seems, however, that this is largely a windows/mac debate. My school changed to Macs last year sometime, and everyone was shocked. Of course, they all ran Windows, except for the Music department (and also Drama). So, I've had over a year to get used to the things (now with Leopard), and I must say that they're not too bad. In fact, there are two things I really like. The first is the side-mouse buttons, which show all the windows. That is really handy. The second is a key which can show the desktop.
Oh, and, actually, I like the ability to invert the colour (Command+Apple+8 off the top of my head).

So, yeah, I have a slight OS lean towards Windows 2000 and Windows XP, because I've used them for the most time (I like XP more, though). However, if given a Mac OS I'd use it*.
*under the condition that I didn't get a computer with it. iMacs are cool, but Macbooks have a low volume, and the Macbook Air is sweet, except it'd break so easily, and has no CD input, and only 1 USB input. I'd get annoyed with that so easily. Oh, and I'd also have to have all the programs that I have now. I need my programs.

#20841 1 2008-07-20T09:18:34Z Weisslenny0
Welcome!
Hey everyone. You now all have access to the Metanet Orchestra sub-forum, and ('cause you're so nice) you can all come into the #Metastra IRC channel. This post contains all there is to know about Metastra, so if you want to get involved our help out, read below. If you want to just check out some of the songs, feel free to browse the topics and post things in them.

About us and projects
Well, the Metanet Orchestra was originally set up by the great Kablizzy, before he left. It's currently moderated mainly by me, but also by Borealis and Sendy, with help from maestro, Yanni, and others.
Our aim was to create music for a game called Knytt Stories. The music was going to be eventually compiled into a ZIP file, so authors could use it on their levels and so on. Also it would just be an opportunity to get some musicians together and see what they could come up with. We're still working on the Knytt Stories music - hopefully it will be done shortly.
Another, more recent projects have come up for us. Animator's game and GamingWolf's game are both in need of music. Currently I am the only on helping out in this area, but other help would be much appreciated.

What you can do to help
If you're a performer, composer, or editor and with to help, please sign in with the respective topic. Please list what you play/use (instrument or program to edit/compose), and I'll hopefully get on to you shortly. You'll be added to the roster, and then assigned things which you can do.
Alternatively, just reply to this if you're unsure on what's happening, or anything like that. If you're really confused and want "face-to-face" talking, you can catch me on the IRC channel (#Metastra).

I think this is all. If there's anything major that I've left out please tell me. Also, if you've got any questions, please ask.

Lenny
